_doc: Scene events: the street around a gig (R. Talsorian, Cyberpunk RED: Single Player Mode, Random Encounters, SPM p.77-84: twelve tables by an area's general security rating and the time of day; the city tables are d100 with 20 rows of 5 points, the Outskirts ones d10 with 10 rows). Read by SceneEvent (src/tactical/scene_event.gd). The roll positions are the book's; every label and note is our own short paraphrase. A gig rolls once when it starts (Campaign._start_gig), from its seed, and keeps the row on the gig (gig.scene_event), so a reload is the same. A row plays when it has no `unmodelled` and only fx keys SceneEvent implements (tests/unit/tactical/test_scene_events.gd): its note is the deploy log line and the ON THE STREET callout; spawning fx put people on the map with the existing systems; `dress` adds set dressing, `sound` and `sky` are view cues only. A scene event is the street around the gig, never a turn of the job itself (that is Twist).

chance._why: HOUSE-RULE (owner: not every gig, about half): a gig has a scene event on a d10 of 1-5. The book rolls when a Beat wants one (SPM p.77).

bands._why: HOUSE-RULE mapping (the book keys by an area's general security rating, SPM p.77; NC2045 Security Codes run 0-11): the street's band is the LOWER of the location's own code and its district's code (a corporate site in the Combat Zone stands on a Combat Zone street); 0-3 Combat Zone, 4-7 Moderate, 8-11 Corporate/Executive. A district drawn as Combat Zone (its profile) is never better than Moderate. Badlands scenes and the Outskirts district use the Outskirts tables; the undercity tunnels have no street and roll none.

times._why: HOUSE-RULE: the book's Day / Night / After Midnight read on the campaign clock (Campaign.minutes, NC2045 p.18 travel already moves it): day 06:00-17:59, night 18:00-23:59, after midnight 00:00-05:59. A tower gig's sky wins: a day sky is day, a night sky is night unless the clock is past midnight.

who._why: Who a `watch` or `gangs` fx puts on the street (factions.json ids). street: the district code's responder (NC2045 p.8; NCPD without one); police: NCPD; gang: one of the district's gangs other than the gig's target (scavvers without one); locals: armed locals; security: generic private security; scavvers, nomads; road_gang: Toecutters (a road gang, NC2045); marshals: the NorCal Marshal Service.

fx._why: text: the log line only. crowd {n, pose, at: street | door | building | vendor}: a cluster of bystanders (Encounter civilians: they panic, block and can be hit). watch {who, n, roam?, at: building | road | door?, near: crowd?}: people on a witness side (neutral until they see a crime: Encounter.witness_side), walking a beat (roam) or holding a spot. gangs {sides: 1 | 2, n, hot, factions?}: a side (or two, at war with each other) at war with everyone who fights (FreeForAll's rule); hot: already shooting (in the initiative order). patrol {n}: more of the site's own people walking the street. trauma {}: a cardholder down on the street and Trauma Team landing for them (Encounter.tt). psycho {maxtac?: [lo, hi] rounds}: a cyberpsycho (the Cyberpsycho block, CPR core p.416) at war with everyone, MaxTac dropping on them after that many rounds. outage: a utility out (Utility Codes, NC2045 p.8). alarm: the alarm starts at that level (1: the site is on edge). dress: set dressing placed as cover (Furnish pieces). sound, sky: view cues.
